dc_eval_cbrn.quote: Red teamers could not successfully compel the model to engineer new biochemical substances.
dc_eval_cbrn.locator: System Card section 2.6 Proliferation of Conventional and Unconventional Weapons
dc_eval_cbrn.note: Red-team findings on nuclear, radiological, biological, chemical domains for this model.

dc_eval_cyber.quote: They found that GPT-4 could explain some vulnerabilities if the source code was small enough to fit in the context window
dc_eval_cyber.note: Contracted experts tested vulnerability discovery and exploitation; found it performed poorly at building exploits.

dc_eval_autonomy.quote: ARC found that the versions of GPT-4 it evaluated were ineffective at the autonomous replication task based on preliminary experiments they conducted.
dc_eval_autonomy.locator: System Card section 2.9 Potential for Risky Emergent Behaviors
dc_eval_autonomy.note: ARC autonomous replication result for early versions; card says final version not tested.

dc_eval_persuasion.quote: Our red teaming results suggest that GPT-4 can rival human propagandists in many domains, especially if teamed with a human editor.
dc_eval_persuasion.locator: System Card section 2.5 Disinformation and Influence Operations

dc_eval_scheming.quote: The model, when prompted to reason out loud, reasons: I should not reveal that I am a robot.
dc_eval_scheming.locator: System Card section 2.9 Potential for Risky Emergent Behaviors
dc_eval_scheming.note: ARC TaskRabbit test: model deceives a human; also tested hiding traces and avoiding shutdown, framed as power-seeking risk. Judgement call between 1 and 2, qualitative finding from a named test.

framework_threshold.note: No safety or scaling framework is named; grep for preparedness, scaling policy, framework finds only OpenAI Evals framework and a hazard analysis paper title. 'safety critical threshold' in Conclusion is a generic precaution, not a named framework.

ext_test_any.quote: These experts had access to early versions of GPT-4 (including GPT-4-early) and to the model with in-development mitigations
ext_test_any.note: External experts red teamed early versions.

ext_test_named_org.quote: We granted the Alignment Research Center (ARC) early access to the models as a part of our expert red teaming efforts

ext_test_government.note: No government body named as testing the model; grep for AISI, safety institute, government shows only usage-policy and acceleration contexts.

ext_test_timing_stated.quote: In August 2022, we began recruiting external experts to qualitatively probe, adversarially test, and generally provide feedback on the GPT-4 models.
ext_test_timing_stated.note: Testing stated as early, before launch (model finished training Aug 2022, launch Mar 2023).

safeguards_training.quote: After the pre-training stage, our primary method for shaping GPT-4-launch behavior was RLHF.

safeguards_runtime.quote: Our automated systems include a suite of machine learning and rule-based classifier detections that identify content that might violate our policies.
safeguards_runtime.locator: System Card section 4.1 Usage Policies and Monitoring

safeguards_access.note: Only generic mention of 'access controls' in a footnote and usage policies; no access restriction tied to risk (no trusted access, KYC, tiers).

safeguards_weights.note: No weight protection described; grep for exfiltrat, weight security finds nothing.
